climate_pressure: Rising heat, rainfall variability and episodic drought/heavy rainfall.
documented_impact: Agricultural production and food availability are sensitive to rainfall and climate shocks.
fcv_mediator: Conflict, displacement, degraded roads, prices and weak purchasing power shape whether production changes translate into household food access.
possible_consequence: Climate-related production losses could worsen acute food insecurity where conflict and market-access constraints limit coping.
geographies: drought concern greater in northern CAR
uncertainty: IPC does not quantify a separate climate causal effect; future drought direction is uncertain.
compact_statement: Climate shocks can affect food production, but whether this produces severe food insecurity in CAR is strongly mediated by conflict, markets, roads, poverty and assistance. (IPCinfo)

climate_pressure: Rainfall variability, drought and pasture/water pressures in CAR and surrounding regions.
documented_impact: Changes in timing or geography of pastoral movements.
fcv_mediator: Weak cross-border regulation, land/water access rules, armed-group involvement and local dispute-management capacity.
possible_consequence: Altered livestock movement may increase the likelihood of localized farmer-herder tensions where regulation and negotiated access are weak.
affected_groups: sedentary farmers and communities along corridors
uncertainty: NUPI explicitly identifies a lack of robust CAR-specific climate-security monitoring.
resilience_factors: compensation arrangements and functioning local mediation
compact_statement: Climate-related mobility pressure can matter, but governance of routes and resources - and armed insecurity - determines whether mobility becomes cooperative, disruptive or violent. (NUPI)

climate_pressure: Drought, rainfall variability and seasonal pasture/water stress.
documented_impact: Pastoralists require mobility and negotiated resource access.
fcv_mediator: Armed violence and state withdrawal can remove route controls, compensation procedures and dispute-resolution mechanisms.
possible_consequence: Climate and seasonal resource stress may become harder to manage peacefully when conflict erodes institutions that previously organized mobility.
uncertainty: Practitioner evidence is not a nationally representative causal study.
compact_statement: Conflict can reduce the institutional capacity needed to manage ordinary and climate-amplified pastoral resource pressures. (NUPI)

climate_pressure: Seasonal flooding and other climate shocks can affect already fragile infrastructure and services.
documented_impact: CAR has large displaced populations; Birao experienced a particularly sharp refugee influx from the Sudan conflict.
fcv_mediator: Conflict-driven displacement increases demand for water, health, shelter, education and livelihoods in low-capacity locations.
possible_consequence: Host areas with large service deficits may have less capacity to absorb an additional flood, drought or food-production shock.
geographies: the mechanism should not be generalized automatically
uncertainty: No reviewed study estimates the marginal effect of displacement on climate-disaster losses in Birao.
resilience_factors: Integration of refugee and host-community services
compact_statement: Conflict-driven population shocks can consume scarce service capacity and plausibly reduce resilience to subsequent climate shocks, but the combined effect has not been directly evaluated.

documented_impact: Agricultural output and food availability vary with rainfall and other shocks.
fcv_mediator: Persistent conflict, displacement and degraded roads restrict market and humanitarian access; high prices and low purchasing power further constrain households.
possible_consequence: A localized climate-related production shock could have larger food-security effects where conflict has already impaired transport and markets.
alternative_explanations: assistance coverage and local harvest conditions
uncertainty: Relative contributions of climate, conflict and market variables are not causally decomposed.
compact_statement: Conflict-damaged access and weak purchasing power can magnify the household consequences of climate-sensitive food-production changes. (IPCinfo)

climate_pressure: Heat, rainfall variability, floods and drought.
documented_impact: Effective adaptation requires observations, risk analysis and water/hydrometeorological information.
fcv_mediator: Weak institutions, limited staff/equipment, fragmented planning and broader fragility constrain data generation and use.
possible_consequence: Poor climate information can reduce the timeliness and targeting of adaptation and disaster-management decisions.
alternative_explanations: Fiscal scarcity and technical constraints may exist independently of armed conflict
uncertainty: Reviewed documents do not estimate the share of climate-information deficits caused specifically by FCV.
compact_statement: Fragile institutional capacity constrains the information systems required to anticipate and manage climate risks, although the specific contribution of conflict is not quantified. (UNFCCC)

documented_impact: Emergency agricultural assistance is intended to protect or restore livelihoods.
fcv_mediator: Weak administrative systems and targeting through formal organizations can shape who receives assistance.
possible_consequence: Programme design can unintentionally leave highly vulnerable households with less support and therefore lower recovery capacity.
uncertainty: Evaluation concerns a 2014-2016 operation, so current programme design may differ.
resilience_factors: Vulnerability-based targeting independent of formal membership
local technical capacity and procurement systems
compact_statement: Independent evaluation demonstrates that delivery rules in a fragile environment can themselves create resilience gaps by excluding vulnerable non-members.

climate_pressure: Seasonal variability in pasture, water and agricultural resources.
documented_impact: Pastoral mobility creates recurring needs for negotiated access to land and water.
fcv_mediator: Local agreements, compensation, regulated routes and farmer-pastoralist exchange can reduce disputes.
possible_consequence: Where legitimate local governance functions, resource variability may be managed through negotiation rather than escalation.
alternative_explanations: Economic complementarity between livestock and crop systems
uncertainty: No experimental or quasi-experimental evaluation was identified.
resilience_factors: reciprocal agricultural-pastoral exchange and local dispute resolution
compact_statement: CAR evidence contains not only risk pathways but also peace-supporting institutions that can mediate resource variability without violence. (ICRC)
